ambiguities.evidence: Eq. (2.3) prints tau = (F - F^epsilon)/epsilon, while Eq. (3.1) adds A^epsilon F^epsilon and Eq. (3.2) prints plus epsilon A^epsilon tau. Algebra using the printed definition would instead produce a minus epsilon A^epsilon tau term. [PDF p. 3, anchor: Eq. (2.3); PDF p. 4, anchor: Eq. (3.1); PDF p. 5, anchor: Eq. (3.2)]
ambiguities.impact: The source contract can preserve the printed expansion and error orders, but the sign of individual perturbation coefficients cannot be chosen consistently without treating one of the displayed signs as a typographical error. [PDF pp. 3-5, anchors: Eqs. (2.3), (3.1), and (3.2)]
ambiguities.issue: The perturbation sign convention is internally inconsistent. [PDF p. 3, anchor: Eq. (2.3); PDF pp. 4-5, anchors: Eqs. (3.1)-(3.3)]

ambiguities.evidence: The paper names E, E_sch, E_per, and Error and gives asymptotic orders, but supplies no exact reference solution, norm, time interval, or uniformity statement in this passage. [PDF p. 5, anchor: paragraph and displays below Eq. (3.3)]
ambiguities.impact: The contract cannot strengthen the result into a quantified norm inequality or select an absolute, relative, componentwise, or final-time interpretation. [PDF p. 5, anchor: error displays below Eq. (3.3)]
ambiguities.issue: The quantities called one-step and global error are not formally defined or normed. [PDF p. 5, anchor: paragraph and displays below Eq. (3.3)]

ambiguities.evidence: Sections 3.1.1 and 3.1.2 later organize algebraic conditions by thresholds on m, but the display below (3.3) does not state whether epsilon is fixed as Delta t tends to zero or whether the O-constants are uniform in epsilon. [PDF p. 5, anchor: displays below Eq. (3.3); PDF pp. 7-8, anchors: Eqs. (3.4)-(3.5)]
ambiguities.impact: No joint-limit theorem or uniform two-parameter bound should be inferred beyond the additive asymptotic form printed by the paper. [PDF p. 5, anchor: displays below Eq. (3.3)]
ambiguities.issue: The domains and quantifier order for p, m, Delta t, and epsilon are not stated in the displayed envelope. [PDF p. 5, anchor: local and global error displays]

contract_plain_english: For the paper's additive Runge-Kutta framework, the second-order B-series expansion separates ordinary scheme terms from terms caused by the approximate operator F^epsilon. [PDF pp. 4-5, anchors: Eqs. (3.1)-(3.3)] If the corresponding consistency and perturbation conditions hold, the paper claims a one-step envelope O(Delta t^(p+1)) + O(epsilon Delta t^(m+1)); only if the perturbed method is stable does it claim the global envelope O(Delta t^p) + O(epsilon Delta t^m). [PDF p. 5, anchor: displays below Eq. (3.3)] The result supplies no norm or uniform constants, and its printed definition of tau has a sign conflict with the printed perturbed rewrite. [PDF p. 3, anchor: Eq. (2.3); PDF p. 5, anchors: Eqs. (3.2)-(3.3)]

source_evidence.anchor: standing stability qualification in the Introduction
source_evidence.observation: The paper analyzes accuracy, does not rigorously analyze mixed-precision stability, and makes its global-error expectations conditional on stability.

source_evidence.anchor: equation (2.3), definition of the perturbation operator
equation (3.1) and the paragraph immediately below it
source_evidence.observation: The general s-stage additive method combines evaluations of F and F^epsilon, and the paper requires F^epsilon(y) - F(y) = O(epsilon) for any y.

source_evidence.anchor: equations (3.2), (3.3), and the displayed local/global error forms below (3.3)
source_evidence.observation: The printed second-order B-series expansion separates terms labeled scheme and perturbation, then states E = E_sch + E_per = O(Delta t^(p+1)) + O(epsilon Delta t^(m+1)) per step and, conditionally on stability, Error = O(Delta t^p) + O(epsilon Delta t^m) globally.

source_evidence.anchor: paragraphs distinguishing well-behaved and chopped perturbations
source_evidence.observation: The paper distinguishes a smooth case, where derivatives of F, F^epsilon, and tau are bounded and cancellation is used, from chopping, where F^epsilon and tau need not be Lipschitz and tau derivatives may not exist.
The indices p and m are determined by separate consistency and perturbation condition families; the nonsmooth perturbation conditions use componentwise absolute-value zero products.

source_evidence.anchor: equation (3.5), perturbation conditions when tau is well behaved
source_evidence.observation: For smooth tau, the perturbation conditions are weaker algebraic cancellation conditions.

statement.algorithm_linkage: The contract applies to the additive mixed-precision Runge-Kutta method (3.1), equivalently represented in the paper by the perturbed form (3.2); it is not a claim about arbitrary numerical algorithms. [PDF pp. 4-5, anchors: Eqs. (3.1)-(3.3)]
binders: The framework binds an s-stage additive Runge-Kutta step with stages y^(i), i = 1,...,s, summation index j = 1,...,s, current step n, step size Delta t, operators F and F^epsilon, and coefficient families A, A^epsilon, b, and b^epsilon. [PDF p. 4, anchor: Eq. (3.1a-b)]

For every state y, the approximation relation is F^epsilon(y) - F(y) = O(epsilon), and tau is introduced as a state-dependent perturbation operator. [PDF p. 4, anchor: paragraph below Eq. (3.1); PDF p. 3, anchor: Eq. (2.3)]

The symbols p and m independently denote the attained scheme-consistency order and perturbation order in the local and global envelopes; the display below (3.3) does not itself state their integer ranges. [PDF p. 5, anchor: paragraph and displays below Eq. (3.3); PDF pp. 7-8, anchors: Eqs. (3.4)-(3.5)]
conclusions: As printed, Eq. (3.3) is u^(n+1) = u^n + Delta t (b-tilde)e F(u^n) + Delta t^2 (b-tilde)(c-tilde) F_y(u^n)F(u^n) + epsilon Delta t {b^epsilon e tau(u^n) + Delta t[b^epsilon(c-tilde) tau_y(u^n)F(u^n) + (b-tilde)c^epsilon F_y(u^n)tau(u^n) + epsilon b^epsilon c^epsilon tau_y(u^n)tau(u^n)]} + O(Delta t^3). [PDF p. 5, anchor: Eq. (3.3)]

The paper explicitly decomposes the one-step error as E = E_sch + E_per, with E_sch the scheme approximation error and E_per the perturbation error. [PDF p. 5, anchor: paragraph immediately below Eq. (3.3)]
Under the corresponding order conditions, the one-step error is E = O(Delta t^(p+1)) + O(epsilon Delta t^(m+1)). [PDF p. 5, anchor: first displayed error form below Eq. (3.3)]
If the method is stable, the expected global error is Error = O(Delta t^p) + O(epsilon Delta t^m). [PDF p. 5, anchor: second displayed error form below Eq. (3.3)]
constants_and_indexing: Stage indices run from 1 to s in both sums of the additive method, and the current and next time levels are n and n+1. [PDF p. 4, anchor: Eq. (3.1a-b)]
The local exponents are p+1 and m+1, while the corresponding stable global exponents are p and m. [PDF p. 5, anchor: local and global error displays below Eq. (3.3)]

The constants hidden by every O-term, their dependence on F, tau, epsilon, final time, and method coefficients, and any uniformity range in Delta t are not stated. [PDF p. 5, anchor: Eq. (3.3) and following error displays]
definitions_and_conventions: The paper defines A-tilde = A + A^epsilon and b-tilde = b + b^epsilon. [PDF p. 5, anchor: sentence below Eq. (3.2)]
The paper prints tau(u) = (F(u) - F^epsilon(u))/epsilon. [PDF p. 3, anchor: Eq. (2.3)]

E_sch and E_per are descriptive components of the one-step error, respectively associated with the F-only scheme terms and the terms involving the perturbation. [PDF p. 5, anchor: labels in Eq. (3.3) and paragraph below it]

The symbols e, c-tilde, and c^epsilon are used in Eq. (3.3) without an explicit definition in that immediate passage; their interpretation as Runge-Kutta abscissa data is inherited from the Butcher framework. [PDF p. 5, anchor: Eqs. (3.2)-(3.3); PDF p. 8, anchor: coefficient discussion in Section 3.2]
error_notions: E, E_sch, and E_per are one-time-step errors, whereas Error denotes the accumulated global error. [PDF p. 5, anchor: paragraph and displays below Eq. (3.3)]

The passage does not give an explicit subtraction defining E or Error against an exact solution, nor does it specify whether the displayed bounds are pointwise, componentwise, or uniform in time. [PDF p. 5, anchor: paragraph and displays below Eq. (3.3)]
exceptional_values: The passage states no assumptions about overflow, underflow, subnormal numbers, NaN, infinity, division by zero, or failed implicit solves. [PDF pp. 4-5, anchors: Eqs. (3.1)-(3.3)]
higher_order_terms: The explicit B-series formula (3.3) ends with a single O(Delta t^3) remainder after retaining terms through second order in Delta t, including terms proportional to epsilon and epsilon^2. [PDF p. 5, anchor: Eq. (3.3)]

The subsequent order envelope suppresses all coefficients and further powers into O(Delta t^(p+1)) and O(epsilon Delta t^(m+1)); it does not claim equality to only two monomials. [PDF p. 5, anchor: first displayed error form below Eq. (3.3)]
hypotheses: The local envelope is conditional on satisfying two separate sets of conditions: classical consistency conditions for the F-only scheme terms and perturbation conditions for the terms containing tau. [PDF p. 5, anchor: paragraph below Eq. (3.3); PDF p. 7, anchor: opening of Section 3.1]
The asserted global envelope additionally requires stability of the perturbed method. [PDF p. 5, anchor: global-error display below Eq. (3.3); PDF p. 2, anchor: standing stability qualification]

Use of the displayed derivative expansion requires the differentiability represented by F_y and tau_y; the paper later separates the bounded-derivative smooth case from chopping, where tau derivatives may fail to exist and stricter conditions must be used. [PDF p. 5, anchor: Eq. (3.3); PDF p. 6, anchor: smooth-versus-chopped perturbation discussion]
implicit_context: The underlying problem is the autonomous ODE u_t = F(u), and u^(n+1) is the numerical Runge-Kutta update rather than notation for the exact ODE solution. [PDF pp. 1-2, anchors: opening ODE and Eq. (1.1)]

The standard s-stage coefficient dimensions are A in s-by-s form and b of length s; Eq. (3.1) gives A^epsilon and b^epsilon the corresponding stage indexing. [PDF p. 2, anchor: sentence after Eq. (1.1); PDF p. 4, anchor: Eq. (3.1)]

The paper's local-to-global order reduction by one power of Delta t is an asserted stable-accumulation conclusion, not an unconditional consequence of the one-step expansion. [PDF p. 5, anchor: local and global error displays; PDF p. 2, anchor: stability qualification]
norms: No vector, matrix, operator, absolute, relative, or componentwise norm is specified for the O-terms or global Error in this passage. [PDF p. 5, anchor: Eq. (3.3) and the two error displays]
numerical_model: The abstract numerical assumption is only F^epsilon(y) - F(y) = O(epsilon) for any y; epsilon scales an operator perturbation rather than being given an IEEE rounding formula. [PDF p. 4, anchor: paragraph below Eq. (3.1)]

The paper motivates F^epsilon through reduced storage precision or a relaxed implicit-solver tolerance, but no unit-roundoff model, rounding mode, or operation-by-operation relative-error law is imposed in the selected framework. [PDF p. 2, anchor: mixed-precision motivation; PDF pp. 4-5, anchors: Eqs. (3.1)-(3.3)]
For chopping, the paper takes F^epsilon = Chop(F), regards F^epsilon as bounded but not Lipschitz, and warns that tau derivatives may not exist. [PDF p. 6, anchor: chopping paragraph]

undebatable_constraints: A faithful contract must preserve the two distinct error sources E_sch and E_per rather than combine them into one undifferentiated O-term. [PDF p. 5, anchor: paragraph below Eq. (3.3)]
The one-step claim has exponents p+1 and m+1, while the stable global claim has exponents p and m. [PDF p. 5, anchor: two displayed error forms below Eq. (3.3)]
The perturbation contribution carries an explicit factor epsilon and has its own order index m, independent of the scheme order p. [PDF p. 5, anchor: Eq. (3.3) and local-error display]
The global result must remain conditional on stability. [PDF p. 5, anchor: sentence introducing the global-error display; PDF p. 2, anchor: stability qualification]

The printed plus signs in Eqs. (3.2)-(3.3) must be reported together with, not silently substituted for, the conflicting sign implied by Eq. (2.3). [PDF p. 3, anchor: Eq. (2.3); PDF pp. 4-5, anchors: Eqs. (3.1)-(3.3)]
